You're working on Nxeon, a Hostinger-clone hosting platform (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres) on a Proxmox server. `/opt/nxeon` is the production working tree (git repo, origin/main on GitHub). `/opt/nxeon-staging` is a separate staging checkout with its own `nxeon_staging` DB, used for verification before anything touches prod.

## Background

Earlier this session, the VPS deploy wizard (`components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx`) was brought to a polished state: a real embedded Stripe Custom Checkout (`PaymentStep.tsx`), a sticky cart bar with a live-updating price baked into its Continue/Deploy button (`WizardStickyCart.tsx`), a reassurance card (`WizardReassuranceCard.tsx`), and — most recently — a billing-term UX fix: previously "Change" next to the billing term term sent the customer all the way back to step 0; now it reveals the term-picker cards inline, right above the payment/summary area, via a `showTermPicker` boolean state toggled by `onChangeTerm`. The billing term row also now shows a "Save X%" discount badge when the selected term carries a discount, via a `discountPercent` field on `PaymentStepSummary`.

Email Hosting, Shared Hosting, and Game Servers wizards were already brought to *partial* parity with VPS earlier this session (real PaymentStep instead of a modal, reassurance cards, review-step restructuring) — but NOT this most recent term-picker-reveal + discount-badge + sticky-cart layer. That's what's still missing, and it's exactly what you're doing now, per explicit instructions from the human running this platform.

## Your task — bring Email Hosting, Shared Hosting, and Game Servers to full parity with VPS on these specific points

Work through these ONE PRODUCT AT A TIME, with full verification after each (see "Verification discipline" below) before moving to the next. Suggested order: Email Hosting, then Game Servers, then Shared Hosting (Shared Hosting's file may be harder to locate — see below).

### 1. Email Hosting (`components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx`, page at `app/dashboard/email/page.tsx`)
- There's a leftover heading/title reading something like "Add email hosting" rendered above the wizard step content (a holdover from before the wizard had its own visual identity). Find and remove it — the wizard's own step indicator/content should carry the visual weight, not a redundant title above it. Check it doesn't leave an orphaned empty wrapper div behind.
- The order summary shows the billing term but not the discount percentage for that term. Add a `discountPercent` computation (mirror how `DeployWizard.tsx` computes `termDiscountPct` — grep it for the exact pattern) and pass it into the `PaymentStepSummary` object the same way VPS does, so a "Save X%" badge shows next to the term when applicable.
- Clicking "Change" next to the billing term currently navigates back to an earlier wizard step. Instead, add a `showTermPicker` boolean state and change `onChangeTerm` to toggle it, then render the same term-picker/cards UI (however Email Hosting's plan-selection step already presents its term options — reuse those cards, don't invent new UI) in a block gated on `showTermPicker`, positioned right above the `<PaymentStep>` block, exactly mirroring `DeployWizard.tsx`'s pattern. Grep `DeployWizard.tsx` for `showTermPicker` to see the exact reference implementation before writing this.
- `WizardStickyCart` (the sticky bottom bar with the live price baked into the Continue/Deploy button) is not wired into this wizard at all. Add it, mirroring exactly how `DeployWizard.tsx` uses it — including making sure the displayed price live-updates when anything that changes `cardCents`/the total changes (see the "sticky cart price bug" note below — this is a REAL regression class that already happened once this session, so check for it explicitly here too).
- On step 1 (the domain step), add a *little* more beginner-friendly explanatory copy — enough that someone unfamiliar with "MX records" or "DNS verification" understands what they're choosing (e.g. what a free subdomain vs. a custom domain means for them in practice), with small inline icons for visual clarity. Do NOT overdo this — a sentence or two per option, not a wall of text. Look at how other steps/wizards in this codebase pair icons with short explainer text for the established visual convention (e.g. `WizardReassuranceCard.tsx`, or the plan-card grids) rather than inventing a new pattern.

### 2. Game Servers (`components/customer/GameDeployWizard.tsx`)
- The order summary currently has NO way to change the billing term at all (no "Change" link/button, no term display, or a static one). Add full parity with VPS: display the term, a discount badge if applicable, and a `showTermPicker`-driven inline reveal (same pattern as above) letting the customer see and pick a different term without leaving the Review step.
- Verify `WizardStickyCart` is present and its displayed price responds correctly to add-on/config changes (this wizard already went through a payment-step migration earlier this session — confirm the sticky cart wasn't missed, and if it's present, still explicitly test that changing any add-on updates its price live).

### 3. Shared Hosting
- Find the actual component — grep the codebase for the Shared Hosting wizard (it wraps a plan step, domain step, install step, add-ons step, review step per an earlier screenshot — search for something like `HostingDeployWizard.tsx` or similar in `components/customer/`, and confirm by checking what `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx` renders for the "hosting" product).
- The "Change" button next to billing term currently sends the customer back to step 1 (the very first step, not just "back one step" — confirm this exactly, it may be worse than the other two products' bugs). Fix it the same way: `showTermPicker` state, inline reveal above payment/summary, no full step navigation.
- Add the discount-percentage badge next to the billing term (same `discountPercent` pattern) if there's a discount for the selected term.
- Add `WizardStickyCart` if it's missing, with the same live-price-on-addon-change requirement as above.

### The "sticky cart price bug" — check for this explicitly everywhere you touch a sticky cart
Earlier this session there was a real bug where `WizardStickyCart`'s displayed price didn't include add-on costs (it only reflected the base plan price), so a customer who added add-ons saw a cart total that didn't match their actual bill. The fix in `DeployWizard.tsx` was to make sure the sticky cart's `priceLabel` prop is computed from the FULL current total (base + IP + extra disk + backup tier + any other add-ons), not just the plan price. When you wire or touch `WizardStickyCart` in any of these three wizards, explicitly verify (by reading the exact prop being passed, and by testing with an add-on selected) that its price includes every add-on that wizard offers — do not assume it's already correct.

## Reference implementation — read this file first
`components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx` is th canonical, already-correct pattern for everything above (term discount badge, `showTermPicker` inline reveal, sticky cart with full-total pricing). `components/customer/PaymentStep.tsx` defines `PaymentStepSummary`'s shape (`discountPercent?`, `promoExplainer?`, `onChangeTerm`) — read both before writing any code so your changes to the other three wizards structurally match rather than reinvent.

## Verification discipline (apply after EACH product, before moving to the next)

1. Before making ANY changes, run `cd /opt/nxeon && npm test 2>&1 | grep "^not ok"` and save that list — this is your baseline. As of this session it was exactly 34 pre-existing failures, all unrelated (pricing/proration/auth/rate-limiting tests), nothing to do with wizard UI. Confirm your own baseline capture matches that shape (pricing/proration/auth-flavored test names, not wizard-flavored) before trusting it.
2. After editing a product's wizard: `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit` must be clean (zero errors).
3. Run `npm test 2>&1 | grep "^not ok"` again — the set of failing test names must be IDENTICAL to your baseline. Any new failure name means your change broke something; fix it before proceeding.
4. Commit with a clear message ending in the two-line trailer:
   ```

   Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
   ```
   Then `git push origin main`. If push fails with "cannot lock ref", wait 2 seconds and retry once — this is a known transient GitHub issue in this repo, not a real conflict.
5. Deploy to staging: `cd /opt/nxeon && bash scripts/deploy-staging.sh main` (this does a real `git fetch` + `reset --hard` in `/opt/nxeon-staging`, `npm install`, `prisma db push`, `npm run build`, and restarts `nxeon-staging-web`/`nxeon-staging-worker`). This can take a couple minutes — if a bash call times out, it continues in the background; check its output file rather than re-running it.
6. Verify LIVE on staging with Playwright (`/opt/nxeon-staging/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs` is the installed playwright — write throwaway `.mjs` scripts, e.g. under `/tmp` or a scratch dir, using `chromium.launch()` + `newContext({ bypassCSP: true })`). Log in with `claude-audit-2026@nxeon.test` / `AuditPass123!` against `https://staging.nxeon.cloud`. For each product's wizard: walk it to the Review/payment step, click "Change" next to the billing term and confirm the term cards reveal INLINE (not a navigation back to an earlier step — check the URL/step indicator didn't change), confirm a discount badge shows when applicable, add an add-on if the product has one and confirm the sticky cart's price updates to include it. Take screenshots to confirm visually, not just via DOM presence checks (styling regressions won't show up in a `.count()` check).
7. Only after all of the above passes for a product, move to the next.

## Hard constraints
- Do **NOT** run `scripts/promote-production.sh` under any circumstances. This is new, unreviewed UI work — production must not be touched. Leave everything on staging only; the human will decide when (and whether) to promote after reviewing it themselves.
- Do not run any build (`npm run build`) inside `/opt/nxeon` itself (the production working tree) — only `tsc --noEmit` and `npm test` are safe there. All real builds happen via `deploy-staging.sh` against `/opt/nxeon-staging`.
- Don't invent new visual patterns — every UI piece you add here already has an established convention somewhere in this codebase (VPS wizard, `WizardReassuranceCard`, existing plan-card grids). Find and reuse it rather than designing something new.
- Don't scope-creep: only touch what's described above. If you notice something else that seems broken while you're in these files, note it in your final report instead of fixing it inline.

## Final report
When done (or if you get blocked on something genuinely ambiguous partway through), report: what you changed per product, the exact verification results (tsc/test-diff status, staging deploy status, what the Playwright screenshots showed), and any open questions or judgment calls you made along the way (e.g. exactly how you phrased the beginner-friendly domain-step copy, or where you found the Shared Hosting wizard file). Keep it concrete and cite file paths/line numbers.
